title: Streaming edge cases notes (SSE) — SDK parity audit scratchpad
content:
Context
- This is a scratchpad of streaming (SSE) edge cases observed during the SDK parity audit.
- Goal: capture “what breaks”, how to reproduce, what signals we have (request-id, error payload), and what we want the cross-SDK behavior to be.
- Not a spec. The spec/decision lives in ADR-0138; this doc is the raw evidence + repros.

Owners / where this is used
- DevEx is using this to drive conformance tests and SDK fixes (python pr-415 / ts pr-289 / go pr-200).
- Support uses it to triage streaming complaints and to ask customers for the right debug info.

Glossary / quick notes
- SSE framing: “event: …\ndata: …\n\n” or just “data: …\n\n” chunks; frames can be split across TCP packets.
- “Mid-stream disconnect” means HTTP connection closes after at least one event has been delivered.
- “Early disconnect” means disconnect happens before any parsable SSE event.

What we ask customers for (minimum debug bundle)
- request-id from response headers (or Redwood error payload if available)
- SDK + version + runtime (Node version; Python requests/httpx version; Go version)
- whether behind proxy (corporate proxy / Cloudflare / Nginx / Envoy / API gateway)
- whether streaming is over HTTP/2, and if any TLS interception is in play
- approximate time to disconnect and whether any tokens were received
- if possible: raw TCP capture is overkill; but “curl -N -v” output is often enough to see buffering / chunking patterns

---

Observed edge cases (by symptom)

1) Partial SSE frames / chunk boundaries split within a line
Symptom
- SDK throws parse error, or silently drops tokens, or stalls waiting for “\n\n”.
- Common when networking stack delivers small chunks (esp. when proxy is involved).

Notes
- We must assume arbitrary splits: "da" + "ta: {json" + "...}\n" etc.
- Also saw split between “\r” and “\n” when intermediaries normalize newlines.

Repro (local)
- Use a simple test server that writes SSE lines one byte at a time:
  - Write: "data: {\"type\":\"delta\",\"token\":\"hel\"}\n"
  - Sleep 10ms
  - Write: "data: {\"type\":\"delta\",\"token\":\"lo\"}\n\n"
- Confirm client emits tokens “hel”, “lo” consistently.

Cross-SDK expectation
- All SDKs must implement an incremental line buffer.
- Never assume read() aligns to lines or frames.

Status
- TS: historically most fragile here when using fetch streams + TextDecoder without careful buffering.
- Python: depends on underlying transport iteration mode; must not treat “chunk” == “line”.
- Go: bufio.Scanner has token length pitfalls; ensure not using default scanner limits for large JSON lines.

2) UTF-8 multibyte characters split across chunks
Symptom
- JSON decode fails (invalid UTF-8), or tokens show replacement characters.

Notes
- We saw this with non-ASCII output (customer prompts in Japanese; emoji in response).
- If the streaming decoder is not configured for streaming decode, splitting a multibyte rune causes decode errors.

Repro
- Prompt that causes non-ASCII output.
- Artificially split response bytes between UTF-8 bytes (test server).

Cross-SDK expectation
- TS: use TextDecoder in streaming mode (decode(chunk, { stream: true })) and preserve undecoded remainder.
- Go: treat the stream as bytes and decode after line assembly (or use a decoder that tolerates split runes).
- Python: ensure incremental decode if doing manual decoding; prefer library mechanisms that handle streaming decode.

3) Proxy buffering / “nothing happens for 30–60s then a burst”
Symptom
- Customer sees “hang” then big burst of tokens, or hits timeouts waiting for first token.
- Often reported as “streaming doesn’t stream”.

Where observed
- SUP-9321: Python SDK appears to hang on streaming; proxy buffering suspected.
- Also heard in sales deep dive (Fireflies ff-89341) that some enterprise networks buffer event streams.

Root causes we’ve seen
- Corporate proxies buffering responses (especially if not recognized as SSE).
- Nginx default buffering (proxy_buffering on).
- Some WAF/CDN products buffer unless specific headers present.

Suggested mitigations (server/platform + docs)
- Ensure we set headers that reduce buffering risk:
  - Content-Type: text/event-stream
  - Cache-Control: no-cache
  - Connection: keep-alive (where applicable)
- Consider documenting Nginx guidance: proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout higher.
- Consider periodic “heartbeat” events (comment lines like “: ping\n\n” or explicit event) to keep intermediaries flushing.

Repro hints
- Put Nginx in front of a test SSE service with default settings; confirm buffering.
- Then set proxy_buffering off and confirm streaming resumes.

Open question
- Do we want to add an official heartbeat interval on the server side, or keep as “best effort / not guaranteed”? ADR-0138 leans toward “SDK must tolerate lack of heartbeats; timeouts should be set appropriately.”

4) Mid-stream disconnect after some tokens (RST/FIN), ambiguous completion
Symptom
- Customer gets partial output and then connection closes without “final” event.
- Some SDKs treat as success (return partial), others throw.

Where observed
- Slack support thread-1739690021: multiple TS streaming disconnect reports.
- Suspected to correlate with mobile networks / NAT timeouts / aggressive load balancers.

What makes it hard
- Without an explicit “done/final” event, client cannot know if model completed.
- Retrying mid-stream is risky (duplicate tokens, different output). Also not obviously idempotent.

Cross-SDK expectation (aligning with ADR-0138 direction)
- If disconnect occurs after any tokens/events have been delivered:
  - Surface an explicit StreamingInterrupted error that includes:
    - whether any events were received
    - number of events/tokens received (best effort)
    - request-id (if known)
  - Do NOT automatically retry by default.
  - Provide a clear escape hatch for application-level retry if they can tolerate duplicates (off by default).

Repro
- Server sends N events then closes socket abruptly (RST if possible).
- Client should raise StreamingInterrupted and include partial text if available (language-specific API choice, but consistent semantics).

5) Early disconnect before first event (connect succeeds, 200 OK, then close)
Symptom
- Looks like “empty stream” or “unexpected EOF”.

Potentially retryable?
- This is the only “streaming retry” case that seems plausibly safe if:
  - no events were delivered
  - request is otherwise safe to retry (GET-like semantics aren’t applicable; it’s POST)
  - we treat it similarly to a transport error before any payload

Cross-SDK expectation (tentative; confirm with SRE + ADR language)
- If zero events received:
  - classify as retryable transport failure (subject to retry budget)
  - ensure we don’t retry forever; respect overall timeout

Notes
- If we do this, we must be careful about requests that might have been processed server-side but failed to stream back. Without idempotency keys, we can’t be sure. This is a known trade-off.

6) Timeouts during streaming (no data for long interval)
Symptom
- Python: “ReadTimeout” or equivalent; TS: fetch AbortError or undici timeout; Go: context deadline exceeded.
- Confusion between “no data yet” vs “stream is stuck”.

Where observed
- SUP-9321 mentions timeouts + buffering.
- SUP-9342 is more about cancel vs timeout, but similar confusion pattern.

What we need
- Distinguish:
  - time to first token (TTFT) timeout
  - idle timeout between events
  - overall request timeout

Repro
- Server delays first event by X seconds.
- Server sends a few events then pauses for Y seconds.

Cross-SDK expectation
- Streaming endpoints should have:
  - a longer overall timeout than non-streaming
  - a sane “idle read” timeout (or no idle timeout by default, but then rely on overall)
- Error mapping should preserve the cause:
  - timeout vs cancellation vs disconnect

7) Cancellation semantics (client abort) are inconsistent across languages
Symptom
- TS: AbortController cancels fetch but stream reader sometimes continues emitting buffered chunks.
- Go: context cancel sometimes returns wrapped error that callers misclassify.
- Python: generator cancellation vs closing response handle leaks connection in some code paths.

Cross-SDK expectation
- Cancellation should be:
  - prompt (stop reading ASAP)
  - deterministic cleanup (close body/connection)
  - reported as a distinct cancellation error type (not timeout, not retryable)

Repro
- Start streaming, read 1–3 events, then cancel.
- Confirm:
  - no more events delivered to user callbacks/iterators
  - underlying HTTP body closed
  - returned error type is Cancellation (or normal completion of iteration with cancellation flag; but must be documented)

8) SSE comments / empty lines / unknown event fields
Symptom
- Parser fails when it encounters:
  - “: keep-alive\n\n” comment lines
  - blank lines
  - “event:” lines with no data
  - data lines with leading spaces

Cross-SDK expectation
- Follow SSE spec tolerance:
  - ignore comments
  - treat blank line as dispatch delimiter
  - ignore unknown fields

Repro
- Inject periodic comment lines and confirm clients ignore.

9) Error payloads during streaming (HTTP 200 but stream contains an error event)
Symptom
- Some gateways/services send 200 then emit an “error” SSE event.
- SDKs differ: some treat as normal event; others throw immediately.

Notes
- We need a consistent rule: if an SSE event indicates error, throw an SDK error with the best possible message + code.
- Must include request-id if present.

Repro
- Stream events: delta, delta, error

Cross-SDK expectation
- On “error” event: raise error and stop iteration.
- Do not retry automatically if any deltas already delivered.

10) Rate limiting / 429 behavior in streaming mode
Symptom
- For non-streaming, 429 is retryable with Retry-After.
- For streaming, most 429s happen before stream starts, but we’ve seen cases where connection upgrades then 429-like payload appears (rare, maybe misrouted).

Where observed
- SUP-9334 is about TS aggressive retries on 429 (not necessarily streaming-only), but customers hit it while using streaming endpoints.

Expectation
- If 429 occurs before first event: treat similarly to normal request (retryable w/ backoff + Retry-After).
- If any streaming data already delivered: do not retry; surface error.

---

Reproduction cookbook (copy/paste)

A) curl sanity check (verify streaming vs buffering)
- curl -N disables stdout buffering.
- Use -v to see headers and whether we’re getting data continuously.

Example:
- curl -N -v \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \
    -d '{"model":"...","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"write 50 short lines"}]}'

If customer reports buffering, ask them to run this from the same environment/network.

B) Node repro snippet (AbortController)
- Start stream, cancel after 2 seconds, confirm no further tokens.
- Important: log timestamps to see if events arrive in bursts.

C) Go repro (context cancel)
- Use context.WithTimeout for overall timeout.
- Use context.WithCancel to cancel mid-stream.
- Ensure we log the error chain.

---

Triage checklist (support + oncall)
- Did the customer receive ANY tokens?
  - Yes -> mid-stream disconnect is not auto-retryable; gather request-id + partial output + time.
  - No -> could be retryable transport failure OR buffering; ask for curl -N output.
- Are they behind an enterprise proxy / TLS interception?
  - If yes, suspect buffering / idle timeouts.
- Are they using the TS SDK on Node 18 vs 20? (fetch/undici differences)
- Are they using a custom HTTP agent/dispatcher?

---

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm with SRE (Rafael/Tomáš) whether “early disconnect before first event” should be retryable by default or opt-in only.
- Decide whether SDKs should expose both:
  - “raw event stream iterator”
  - “text accumulator helper”
  and how errors carry partial text without encouraging unsafe retries.
- Conformance tests to add (Leila/Sahana)
  - partial line splitting
  - multibyte UTF-8 split
  - server sends comment lines
  - mid-stream disconnect after N events
  - cancel mid-stream (assert cleanup)
  - proxy buffering simulation (harder in CI; maybe a dedicated integration test)

Appendix: pointers
- Most relevant threads
  - Slack devex thread-1739639922 (partial frames + proxy discussion)
  - Slack support thread-1739690021 (TS disconnect escalation)
- Most relevant tickets
  - SUP-9321 (Python hang / buffering suspicion)
  - SUP-9342 (Go timeout vs cancel inconsistency)
  - SUP-9334 (retry amplification on 429; impacts streaming customers too)
